title: OSS MLflow UI QueryClient: build with createMlflowQueryClient so queries run while navigator.onLine is false
answers: Why does the MLflow UI show a blank loading skeleton and make no API calls even though the server responds?
Where is the React Query client for the OSS MLflow UI and the model trace notebook renderer created?
If I add a new top-level query in the OSS UI, will it still run when the browser reports offline?
Why does the notebook trace explorer hang on a skeleton when navigator.onLine is false?
body:
Path: shared/web-shared/query-client/createMlflowQueryClient.ts:createMlflowQueryClient builds the QueryClient for both OSS entry points: the main app shell (src/app.tsx:MLFlowRoot) and the standalone model trace notebook renderer (shared/web-shared/model-trace-explorer/oss-notebook-renderer/bootstrap.tsx:AppComponent). Every MLflow UI query, including the serverInfo query that gates router creation, passes through it.
Rule: Create OSS query clients through createMlflowQueryClient, not a bare `new QueryClient()`. It sets defaultOptions.queries.networkMode to 'always'. React Query's default 'online' mode pauses a query before queryFn runs whenever navigator.onLine is false, and that flag can latch false while the server is reachable.
Symptom: With navigator.onLine reporting false, the UI stayed on a loading skeleton with empty #root and zero API requests. No error or console output, and the same server returned 200 to fetch() from the page console. The notebook trace explorer hung the same way.
Constraints: Setting networkMode only on the serverInfo query is not enough; other data queries stay paused and the page renders empty tables. The default is applied client-wide on purpose. This is a deliberate exception to the no-singleton-query-client lint rule, which the factory disables inline.
applies: OSS MLflow UI and notebook trace renderer under mlflow/server/js/src; does not cover Databricks-internal clients that build their own QueryClient.
says: The tracking web interface hangs indefinitely on a blank loading skeleton without loading data.
Notebook trace explorer gets stuck on a loading screen when working without internet access.
The dashboard displays empty tables and stops requesting data when the browser detects offline status.
Make the web console connect to local servers even when disconnected from the internet.
search: In mlflow/server/js/src, QueryClient instances for the open-source MLflow UI shell (app.tsx:MLFlowRoot) and notebook trace renderer (bootstrap.tsx:AppComponent) must be constructed with createMlflowQueryClient. The factory configures defaultOptions.queries.networkMode to 'always', ensuring queries run even when navigator.onLine latches false. This client-wide default applies across all OSS queries, but does not cover Databricks-internal query clients.
